title: California Civil Code section 9560 - Notice required to enforce a claim against a public works payment bond
claims: Section 9560(a) provides that, in order to enforce a claim against a payment bond, a claimant shall give the preliminary notice provided in Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 9300).

Section 9560(b) provides that, if preliminary notice was not given as provided in Chapter 3, a claimant may enforce a claim by giving written notice to the surety and the bond principal within 15 days after recordation of a notice of completion, and that if no notice of completion has been recorded, the time for giving that written notice is extended to 75 days after completion of the work of improvement.

Section 9560(c) provides that, commencing July 1, 2012, and except as provided in subdivision (b), if the preliminary notice was required to be given by a person who has no direct contractual relationship with the contractor, and who has not given notice as provided in Chapter 3, that person may enforce a claim by giving written notice to the surety and the bond principal, as provided in Section 9562, within 15 days after recordation of a notice of completion, or within 75 days after completion of the work of improvement if no notice of completion has been recorded.

Section 9560(d) provides that subdivision (c) does not apply where all progress payments, except for those disputed in good faith, have been made to a subcontractor who has a direct contractual relationship with the general contractor to whom the claimant has provided materials or services, or where that subcontractor has been terminated from the project pursuant to the contract and all progress payments, except those disputed in good faith, have been made as of the termination date.
Section 9560(e) provides that, pursuant to Section 9300, the section does not apply to a laborer, as defined under Section 8024.
notes: Fetched 2026-09-30 from the publisher's own site and read in full. Subdivision (d) is the branch most easily missed: the late-notice route in (c) is unavailable once the claimant's subcontractor has been paid its progress payments, or was terminated and paid to the termination date. Chapter 3 (section 9300 onward) was not read for this record, so the content and timing of the preliminary notice itself are not described. Section 9562 says notice under section 9560 must comply with Chapter 2 (commencing with section 8100) of Title 1, which was also not read.
